newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO VIEW - China Eastern, a rare China airline play.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW - China Eastern, a rare China airline play.

text.p: The first overseas offering of a Chinese airline in Hong Kong in the coming week will give investors a rare opportunity to invest in China's promising aviation sector, analysts said.

China Eastern Airlines Corp Ltd of Shanghai is expected to kick off its 140 million H-share initial public offering (IPO) in Hong Kong on January 28, offering shares at between HK$1.24 to HK$1.39 each, market sources said.
H-shares are shares of Chinese enterprises listed in Hong Kong.
"Being the first airline among the H-share sector, investment funds are expected to show strong interest in the shares," said Deon Lo, senior aviation analyst at Seapower Research.

A research report by Morgan Stanley, which is expected to be the global co-ordinator of the issue, said that China Eastern is one of the most profitable and best-managed airlines in China and is bound to benefit from an expected 15-percent annual increase in aviation traffic over the next decade.

The airline is also well-positioned to exploit rapid growth in international air links as Shanghai grows into the Chinese government's favoured international economic, financial and trading centre for the country, Morgan Stanley said.
"It sounds like it is one of the most attractive potential airlines that exist," said an aviation analyst at a regional brokerage.

China Eastern will raise about US$200 million through a dual listing in Hong Kong and New York, with 90 percent of the issue placed internationally and the remaining 10 percent publicly available in Hong Kong.

China Eastern filed earlier this month with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to sell 12.6 million American Depositary Shares (ADS) at US$16 to US$18 each. The ADS issue represents 1.26 billion H-shares of the airline.
Dealing in the Hong Kong H-shares is expected to begin on February 5, sources said.

Analysts said that while China Eastern can expect strong initial demand from overseas investors, a relatively high debt-to-equity ratio of about 10:1 and tough competition from Hong Kong-based Dragonair could dampen longer-term prospects.

"The debt ratio is seen a bit high compared with other counterparts. I think a ratio of between one to two times is healthy and comfortable (for an airline)," said an analyst at MeesPierson Securities.
Morgan Stanley suggested that China Eastern's debt-to-equity ratio could be halved if new equity is raised.
The report also projects net earnings to rise 10.3 percent to 604.9 million yuan this year after a 13 percent decline in 1996 to 549 million yuan, due to high operating costs and tough competition.

"China Eastern is seen having keen competition from parallel flights operated by Dragonair," said one analyst. "Dragonair is seen even more promising in view of its relatively low gearing if it seeks a listing later."
China Eastern's float is expected to pave the way for other competitors, such as China Southern Airlines, one of six major airlines that dominate CHina's aviation industry.
By the end of 1996, China Eastern had a total of 120 routes, including international, regional and domestic.
It flies to 13 major international cities in nine countries and six new international destinations are expected to be added in the next two years, the Morgan Stanley report said.
